title: Neighborhood Shadow Ledger
tests: Data-as-artifact example: a fictional city-block light and shadow dataset rendered as a believable municipal field ledger with maps, gauges, stamps, sample packets, and handled archival materials.
prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram
Asset type: GPT Image 2 data-as-artifact archive image
Primary request: Create a vertical 1024x1536 polished image titled conceptually "Neighborhood Shadow Ledger" where fictional daily light-and-shadow data has been turned into a believable physical civic artifact.

Scene/backdrop: a careful overhead studio photograph of an opened municipal field ledger resting on a worn oak planning desk, surrounded by small brass measuring tools, translucent acetate overlays, sun-path strings, annotated vellum tabs, a pocket sundial, pencil shavings, and tiny sample envelopes of street dust and leaf fragments. The object should feel archived, handled, and useful, not like a generic poster.

Subject and information design: the ledger page records one imaginary city block across a full day. Make the data visible as an artifact: a foldout block map with shadow bands stretching from buildings, small hourly sun-position stamps, a vertical strip of tree-canopy silhouettes, a little receipt-like column of "minutes of shade," a porch-warmth gauge, and a few museum-label callouts. Include only short, large, readable labels such as "SHADOW LEDGER", "06:00", "NOON", "18:00", "TREE SHADE", "BRICK HEAT", and "COOL WALK". Other fine marks may be decorative pseudo-notation and do not need to be readable.

Composition/framing: vertical 9:16, photographed straight down with slight lens depth and real page curvature. The ledger occupies most of the frame, but the surrounding tools make it obvious this is a physical artifact. Use layered paper edges, cotton rag texture, stamped ink, thin red and cyan pencil routes, brass clips, index tabs, and translucent overlays casting faint shadows.

Lighting/mood: late afternoon window light crossing the desk, warm highlights on brass, cool blue-gray shadow ink, cream paper, brick red accents, graphite smudges, subtle dust, crisp tactile detail. It should feel like data someone could file in a drawer and care about later.

Constraints: no real logos, no brand names, no watermark, no signature, no tiny unreadable wall of text, no app UI, no generic glossy AI concept art, no copyrighted characters, no people, no dancing or implied performance. Prioritize readable hierarchy and physical plausibility.

artifact.description: A fictional municipal field ledger that turns daily light, heat, walking comfort, and street material samples into a handled planning artifact.
artifact.continuity: Data as Artifact images treat information as something filed, carried, measured, stamped, repaired, or displayed in the physical world.

title: Household Noise Thermometer
tests: Data-as-artifact example: fictional room-by-room household sound data embodied as a vintage tabletop instrument with gauge, room dial, pins, ticker tape, vials, and calibration ephemera.
prompt:
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: GPT Image 2 data-as-artifact archive image
Primary request: Create a square 1024x1024 polished image titled conceptually "Household Noise Thermometer", where a fictional day's room-by-room sound data has been embodied as a believable vintage tabletop instrument rather than a chart or poster.

Scene/backdrop: a close studio photograph of a compact mid-century desktop measuring instrument on a kitchen counter at dusk. It should look like an object someone could have bought from a municipal home-science catalog: brushed enamel body, bakelite knobs, glass meter window, paper roll slot, tiny brass feet, and a few detachable colored room tokens beside it. No people.

Subject and information design: the instrument translates household sound into physical readings. It has a large analog needle gauge labeled "HOUSEHOLD NOISE", a segmented dial with room labels such as "KITCHEN", "HALL", "BEDROOM", "WINDOW", and "CELLAR", colored pins showing quiet/active periods, a small ticker-tape strip emerging from the side with simplified marks, and a row of small glass vials filled to different levels like captured sound samples. Use only short readable labels: "HOUSEHOLD NOISE", "QUIET", "ACTIVE", "KITCHEN", "HALL", "BEDROOM", "WINDOW", "CELLAR". Other fine marks may be decorative pseudo-notation.

Composition/framing: square product-style photo, three-quarter view from slightly above, instrument centered but surrounded by meaningful parts: room tokens, a calibration card, coiled cloth cord, two tiny screwdrivers, a folded guarantee slip, and soft reflections on the counter. The data should feel baked into the object through needles, pins, vials, dials, and ticker tape, not printed as a flat infographic.

Lighting/mood: warm kitchen dusk light with cool blue window reflection, enamel cream, muted teal, burgundy pin marks, aged brass, black bakelite, glass highlights, subtle wear, dust in seams, crisp tactile detail, plausible manufacturing design.

Constraints: no real logos, no brand names, no app UI, no smartphone, no people, no watermark, no signature, no generic glossy sci-fi dashboard, no dense tiny text, no copyrighted characters, no dancing or performance imagery. Make the artifact immediately understandable at a glance.

artifact.description: A fictional tabletop instrument that turns room-by-room household sound data into needles, pins, vials, dials, and ticker tape.

title: Sleep Debt Boarding Pass
tests: Data-as-artifact example under the revised rule: fictional sleep and wake measurements embodied as issued travel paperwork, punched cards, delay notices, route slips, baggage tags, and lost-hours coupons.
prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual
Asset type: GPT Image 2 data-as-artifact archive image
Primary request: Create a polished 1024x1536 vertical data-as-artifact image titled conceptually "Sleep Debt Boarding Pass", where a fictional week's sleep/wake measurements have become a travel packet someone could hold, file, stamp, and carry.

Scene/backdrop: an overhead archival photograph of a small travel-document packet on a dark train-station counter at night. The packet includes a boarding pass, baggage tag, delay notice, route slip, punched transfer card, and a small envelope of "lost hours" coupons. The artifact should feel issued by a sleepy fictional transit office, handled, creased, stamped, and practical.

Subject and information design: the data is the object. Encode seven nights of fictional sleep debt as travel paperwork: departure times become station stops, wakeups become punched interruptions, naps become transfer slips, total deficit becomes a baggage weight, and recovery sleep becomes a delayed arrival stamp. Include sparse large readable labels only: "SLEEP DEBT", "BOARDING PASS", "LOST HOURS", "DELAY", "TRANSFER", "ARRIVAL", "7 NIGHTS". Other small numbers and marks can be believable pseudo-notation.

Composition/framing: vertical 9:16, straight-down but with real paper thickness and shadows. The boarding pass should be the largest item, diagonally placed, with smaller slips tucked under it. Use perforated edges, punched holes, station-stamp circles, red cancellation marks, carbon-copy blue ink, rubber-stamp texture, torn envelope flap, paper fibers, and a worn brass paper clip. Make it immediately obvious as a data-bearing travel artifact, not a poster and not an electronic interface.

Lighting/mood: dim station-window light, warm desk lamp edge, midnight blues, faded cream ticket stock, red stamp ink, blue carbon copy, soft graphite smudges, tactile shadows, crisp readable hierarchy, slightly melancholic but charming.

Constraints: no measuring device, no dashboard, no control panel, no smartphone, no app UI, no generic infographic poster, no real logos, no brand names, no watermark, no signature, no dense tiny text, no people, no copyrighted characters, no dancing or performance imagery. The world's measurements must visibly become the paperwork itself.

artifact.description: A fictional week of sleep and wake measurements turned into issued travel paperwork: boarding pass, route slip, delay notice, transfer card, baggage tag, and lost-hours coupons.
artifact.continuity: Data as Artifact images treat information as something filed, carried, measured, stamped, repaired, or displayed in the physical world.
